## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

ProfileRepository — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/profile/ProfileRepository.kt

## Trigger

ProfileSyncPushService.applyIncoming calling applyProfile, itself
triggered by a confirmed incoming payload — observed

## Today

`ProfileSyncPushService.applyProfile` (ProfileSyncPushService.kt:70-83)
applies the incoming profile's five settable fields through five
separate calls to `ProfileRepository`: `updateHrMaxBpm`, one
`updateZoneThreshold` per index in a loop, `updateExpectedDistanceM`,
`updateLongPressMs`, `updateCorrectionFactor`. Each of these, in
`ProfileRepositoryImpl` (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/profile/ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt),
reads the whole current row through `currentOrDefault()`
(`runBlocking { profileDao.observe().first() }`), copies one field on
it, and writes the whole row back through `write()`
(`profileDao.upsert(profile.toEntity())`) — a read-modify-write with
no transaction and no lock spanning the five calls, nor even a single
one of them. `ProfileDao.upsert` (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/ProfileDao.kt)
is a plain `@Insert(onConflict = REPLACE)`, run once per call, not
wrapped in a `@Transaction`. A local edit (e.g. through
`ProfileViewModel`'s own updaters on the phone, or any writer on the
watch) landing between two of `applyProfile`'s five calls reads a row
that already reflects the incoming payload's earlier fields and writes
its own field back over the whole row, silently discarding whichever
of the two — the local edit or a later field from the incoming
payload — loses the race.

## Expected

`ProfileRepository` exposes one operation that writes the incoming
profile's five settable fields as a single atomic unit — one read of
the current row (only where a value depends on it, e.g. validation),
one write of the whole row, wrapped in a Room `@Transaction` the way
`RaceDao.upsert` already is (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/RaceDao.kt:43-44).
`ProfileSyncPushService.applyProfile` calls this single operation
instead of the five independent updater calls, so no local edit can
observe or overwrite a partially-applied incoming profile.
